title: Houdin's theory that the Great Pyramid was built from the inside out (internal ramp)

tellings.quote: Houdan in in in France saying that it was built from the inside out.

French architect Jean-Pierre Houdin suggests that an internal ramp spiraling within the pyramid structure itself carried the blocks. This is an idea that gained renewed interest after the Scan Pyramids project detected unexplained voids inside the Great Pyramid.
tellings.difference: Links the theory to the voids that ScanPyramids detected.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell Houdin's theory that the Great Pyramid was built from the inside, by an internal ramp.

as_told.title: Houdin's internal ramp theory and the ScanPyramids voids

tellings.quote: And you have people like I think Jean-Pierre Houdin in France who say that there is something about like, you know, internally like the blocks get pulled up or something.

tellings.link_reason: Both tell Jean-Pierre Houdin's theory that the Great Pyramid was built from the inside, with blocks moved up internally.

as_told.title: Pyramid internal ramp theory and older dating

plain: The French architect Jean-Pierre Houdin thinks the Great Pyramid at Giza was built from the inside out, with the blocks hauled up a ramp that spirals inside the pyramid itself. Michels brings this up himself in four episodes and calls Houdin one of the leading researchers on how the pyramid was built. Once he says the idea got new attention after ScanPyramids, a project that scanned the pyramid, found unexplained empty spaces inside it, and another time he simply says the blocks were somehow pulled up from inside. If Houdin is right, it would explain how the huge blocks were lifted.
